Instinct Gets the Full Financial Picture With Plaid
summary:
People are increasingly navigating their financial lives with AI every day. Now, Plaid is powering read-only financial account connectivity for Instinct. Instinct is a personal assistant that works where people already interact: through iMessage and WhatsApp. With Plaid, U.S. consumers can securely connect their financial data to Instinct for personalized conversations in a familiar interface. Instinct joins more than 800 AI-native startups building with Plaid. 
What Plaid makes possible within Instinct
Plaid paved the way for secure, consumer-permissioned data sharing in U.S. open finance. Now, we are applying the same trusted infrastructure, used by 1 in 2 U.S. consumers with a bank account, to deliver real-time financial insights to thousands of U.S. Instinct users. 
Instinct is quickly emerging as an option for consumers who want a personal assistant in their pocket, with 35% of users connecting a personal credit card within three weeks. Once a user has created an Instinct account, they can ask their assistant financial questions directly in iMessage or WhatsApp. Instinct will then prompt a user to authenticate their financial accounts through Plaid for more personalized answers. From there, Instinct can read the accounts alongside other helpful connections, like email and calendar. Instinct can help track refunds, follow up on HSA reimbursements, and plan a personalized holiday budget.
Instinct reads balances and transactions to spot patterns, make recommendations, and proactively flag what needs attention. Here are a couple other scenarios:
Splitting grocery bills with a roommate: “Help me split the last three grocery orders into two separate expenses.” Instinct finds the orders, works out who owes what, and messages each roommate their share. 
Proactively managing duplicate charges: “It looks like the hotel charged you twice, but your confirmation email only shows one night. Want me to draft the dispute?” Instinct asks for approval before taking any next steps.
Building a better financial future 
In addition to Instinct, Plaid is helping consumers securely connect their financial data to other AI platforms like ChatGPT, Claude, Google Gemini, Grok, Muse, and Perplexity’s Personal CFO, which recently expanded to Europe. People who have never tried a budgeting app are finding help from assistants that can understand them holistically and share tailored financial guidance. Of users who choose to connect more than one bank account to an AI platform with Plaid, 75% connect a second bank account within 1 day, and 65% do so within one hour. These users are also choosing to keep more than 95% of their connections active, indicating that they are finding daily value in their experiences.

content: Plaid is partnering with Instinct to power read-only financial account connectivity for the AI-native personal assistant. Operating through iMessage and WhatsApp, Instinct allows U.S. consumers to securely connect their financial data using Plaid's trusted infrastructure. The integration enables personalized conversations and real-time financial insights, helping users track expenses, manage budgets, and spot spending patterns directly within familiar messaging interfaces.

title: ANZ Completes Major Cloud Data Transformation, Strengthening Data Foundations to Improve Customer Experiences
summary:
ANZ has completed the migration of one of its largest data platforms to Amazon Web Services (AWS), establishing a modern, scalable foundation to support the bank's growing use of data, analytics and AI.
The new cloud-based platform strengthens ANZ's ability to manage and protect customer information through enhanced security controls through a modern cloud architecture.
The Enterprise Big Data platform, which supports services across payments, business banking and customer remediation, was migrated from an on-premises environment to Amazon EMR, a managed cluster platform that simplifies running big data frameworks. The transformation moved 1.7 petabytes of data, equivalent to more than 340 million smartphone photos, across 300 million files, 142,000 tables, 4,500 automated data workflows and 4,000 views. 
The migration was completed in six months instead of an anticipated 18 months using AI-assisted engineering to help analyse, convert, test and optimise workloads. Engineers used a troubleshooting AI assistant powered by Amazon Bedrock to identify and fix performance bottlenecks using the chatbot, without needing to manually comb through code and configurations saving time.
By applying agentic AI across discovery and migration activities, ANZ reduced migration effort by an estimated 35 per cent compared with traditional approaches and reduced defects and rework by approximately 50 per cent through testing and validation. 
The new platform provides greater scalability and resilience while unlocking new opportunities to improve customer and employee experiences. 
ANZ Group Chief Information Officer Donald Patra said: "This transformation strengthens our technology foundations to make banking better and simpler for our customers. It also demonstrates how AI-assisted engineering can accelerate complex delivery while maintaining a disciplined focus on security, resilience and quality.”
A standout feature of the program was how ANZ and AWS Professional Services engineers used AI to accelerate delivery and improve outcomes.
The solution processed data at approximately seven times faster than an initial alternative approach, has already tokenised almost 80 terabytes of data and reduced operating costs from more than US$10,000 per day to less than US$3,000 per month.
ANZ Chief Data and AI Officer Kai Yang said: "Data is the foundation of modern banking and increasingly the foundation of AI. As we explore new ways to use data and analytics to improve customer and employee experiences, having modern, scalable and secure infrastructure is critical.
"This transformation modernises one of ANZ's most important data platforms and provides a stronger foundation for future innovation. It gives us greater flexibility to scale and simplify our technology environment and accelerate the development of new data and capabilities over time.
"Completing a program of this scale in six months demonstrates what can be achieved when technology, people and AI-assisted engineering come together behind a shared goal."
AWS Managing Director for Australia and New Zealand, Chris Casey said: "Migrating a major banking data platform while it continues to serve customers in real time is one of the most complex undertakings in financial services. Completing a migration of this scale in six months reflects the trust and world-class delivery capability of AWS Professional Services, AWS Partners, and the team at ANZ.
"It’s great to see ANZ using agentic AI to handle time-consuming processes that previously took months, giving the teams more time to focus on the complex work that needed expertise and human judgement."

content: ANZ has completed a major cloud data transformation by migrating one of its largest data platforms to Amazon Web Services.
